primitives.name: Wearable sensor-based pain monitoring
primitives.verbatim_quote: Wearable technologies provide real-time biomechanical and physiological data, including movement asymmetry, joint loading, gait deviation, fatigue, and recovery status.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Movement asymmetry (dimensionless), Joint loading (N/m²), Gait deviation (meters), Fatigue (arbitrary units), Recovery status (binary indicator)
primitives.assumptions: Assumes linear relationship between sensor readings and underlying biomechanical states, constant sensor calibration, and normal distribution of measurement noise.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails when sensor drift exceeds ±5% over 24 hours or when biomechanical states exhibit non-linear dynamics.

layer2.telemetry: Real-time biomechanical and physiological time-series data

primitives.name: Computer vision-based motion analysis
primitives.verbatim_quote: Computer vision and pose estimation support non-invasive analysis of posture, motion quality, compensatory movement, and exercise performance.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Pose angles (radians), Motion quality score (0-100 scale), Compensatory movement index (dimensionless), Exercise performance metrics (e.g., repetitions, velocity)
primitives.assumptions: Assumes stable lighting conditions, clear line-of-sight, and accurate calibration of camera parameters. Ignores occlusions and low-resolution imagery.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Degradation occurs when occlusion rate exceeds 15% or when camera resolution drops below 1080p.

layer2.telemetry: Non-invasive posture and motion feature vectors

primitives.name: Predictive analytics for injury risk
primitives.verbatim_quote: Predictive analytics and machine learning models may identify injury risk patterns, guide rehabilitation progression, and assist return-to-play decision-making.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Injury risk probability (0-1), Rehabilitation progress score (0-100 scale), Return-to-play readiness index (dimensionless)
primitives.assumptions: Assumes ergodicity of training data, stationary injury risk factors, and sufficient labeled examples for model training. Ignores sudden rule changes.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure mode triggered by concept drift in injury patterns or insufficient historical data for rare events.

layer2.telemetry: Historical injury and performance time-series data

primitives.name: Multimodal sensor fusion
primitives.verbatim_quote: Multimodal sensor fusion further strengthens pain monitoring by combining clinical, behavioral, biomechanical, physiological, and athlete-reported data into more comprehensive decision-support systems.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Clinical data (binary/nominal), Behavioral data (Likert scale), Biomechanical data (SI units), Physiological data (SI units), Athlete-reported data (Likert scale)
primitives.assumptions: Assumes independent information sources, additive noise structure, and linear combination of modalities. Ignores non-additive interactions.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down when modalities are highly correlated (>0.95) or when fusion rules are mis-specified.

Wearable sensors provide high-frequency biomechanical measurements, while computer vision offers holistic motion analysis. Predictive models integrate these signals to forecast injury risk, but require robust fusion frameworks to avoid information redundancy. These primitives form a hierarchical Bayesian network where sensor observations inform latent injury states, enabling conformal prediction intervals for decision-makers.
